response.sql: WITH group_avgs AS (SELECT oe.ordersmark, o.orderflow, AVG(oe.fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions oe JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = oe.ordersmark WHERE oe.expirespot BETWEEN '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY oe.ordersmark, o.orderflow) SELECT AVG(avg_fill) AS avg_of_group_averages FROM group_avgs;

assumptions.assumption: The inner JOIN drops executions with no matching order, and each recordvault matches at most one order, so no execution is double-counted.

expirespot is compared as text using BETWEEN, which is inclusive at both ends and uses lexicographic string ordering. The schema types expirespot as text(6), while the documentation describes it as a timestamp, so the stored strings are assumed to share the '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' format.

AVG ignores NULL fillcount values inside each group, and a group whose fillcount values are all NULL yields a NULL average that the outer AVG also ignores. A NULL orderflow forms its own status group rather than being dropped.
